title: Pyramid Texts of Unas: Utterances 72-116 (sarcophagus chamber, north wall, middle register)
source: Pyramid of Unas, Saqqara, sarcophagus chamber, north wall, middle register (photograph: L. F. Husson for A. Piankoff 1968, via Pyramid Texts Online) + TLA transliteration (ed. D. Topmann, CC BY-SA 4.0) + English of S. A. B. Mercer (1952, public domain in the US)
description: The Pyramid Texts on the north wall, middle register of the sarcophagus chamber in the pyramid of Unas (c. 2350 BCE), utterance by utterance, with the TLA transliteration and Mercer's English.
introduction:
The Pyramid Texts are the oldest large body of Egyptian religious writing: spells, called utterances, for the resurrection of the dead king, his protection, his meals and his ascent to the sky, cut in vertical columns of hieroglyphs on the walls of the burial apartments of late Old Kingdom pyramids. The pyramid of Unas at Saqqara, the last king of the 5th Dynasty (about 2375-2345 BCE), is the first to carry them. Its sarcophagus chamber, the passage to the antechamber, the antechamber and the corridor hold 649 numbered columns of text; this library gives every column, wall by wall, in seventeen entries (227 different utterances, some of them inscribed more than once).

This entry is the north wall, middle register of the sarcophagus chamber: 55 columns of hieroglyphs, Sethe's W 56-109, which follow each other from the left-hand (west) edge of the photograph. It holds the utterances 72, 73, 74, 75, 76, 77, 78, 79, 81, 25, 32, 82, 83, 84, 85, 86, 87, 88, 89, 90, 91, 92, 93, 94, 95, 96, 108, 109, 110, 111, 112, 113, 114, 115, 116. The TLA numbers one extra column in PT 77 as 61+1.

Each section is one utterance. The Egyptian is the transliteration of the Thesaurus Linguae Aegyptiae (edition by Doris Topmann), with Sethe's Unas column number (W) before each column; a number ending in 'a' marks the offering label at the foot of a column. Signs restored by the editor are in square brackets, signs the scribe left out in angle brackets, damaged signs in half brackets. The English is Samuel A. B. Mercer's translation of 1952. Mercer translates Sethe's composite text made from all the pyramids that have an utterance, so his wording can include clauses that are not in the Unas copy, and his section numbers (134a, 134b ...) are Sethe's paragraph numbers, not column numbers; he writes 'N.' where the wall has the king's name. The photograph shows the whole wall; each section's note gives its columns counted from the edge where the text on that wall begins.
translator_notes: Mercer's separate headings, postscripts and variants taken from other pyramids are left out.
Letters follow the sacred-texts transcription of Mercer: ȝ stands for aleph and ‘ for ayin; letters underlined in the printed book are given as ḏ, ṯ, ẖ.
Sethe's section numbers are kept as printed in that transcription, including a few misprints (for example '146.' for 141b in Utterance 215).
The TLA has no hieroglyphic encoding for these texts, so only the transliteration is shown.

56aAwake thou in peace, (as) Tȝi.t awakes, in peace, (as) Tȝit.t (she of Tȝi.t) awakes in peace,
56b(as) the eye of Horus in Buto (awakes) in peace, (as) the eye of Horus which is in the houses of the Lower Egyptian crown (awakes) in peace,
56c(the eye) which the weavers wove (?), (the eye) which the sedan-chairman planned (?).
57aCause thou (0 Eye) the two lands to bow to N., as they bow to Horus,.
57bCause the two lands to fear N., as they fear Set.
57cSit thou before N., as his god; open thou his way before the spirits,
57dthat be may stand before the spirits like Anubis, "First of the Westerners."
57eTo say four times: Forward, forward to Osiris. Two rolls of linen.

22aThis is thy cool water, Osiris; this is thy cool water, O N., which went forth from thy son, which went forth from Horus.
22bI have come; I have brought to thee the eye of Horus, that thy heart may be refreshed by it. I have brought it to thee. It is under thy soles.
23aTake to thyself the efflux (sweat), which goes forth from thee; thy heart shall not be weary thereby.
23bTo say four times, when thou goest forth justified: Libation; two pellets of natron.

translation.text:
62aTo lift up before his face. To say: Lift up thy face, Osiris; lift up thy face, O N., whose spirit hastens.
62bLift up thy face, N., be mighty, be sharp (pre-eminent?),
62cthat thou mayest see that which cometh forth from thee. Praise it (?); partake in it.
63aWash thyself, N.; open thy mouth with the eye of Horus.
63bSummons, thy ka, like Osiris, that he may protect thee from all anger of the dead.
63cN., receive thy bread, even the eye of Horus. To deposit (an offering) on the ground before him.
